title: A Common Blood Pressure Drug Could Supercharge a Cancer Therapy
hook: Telmisartan, a widely used blood pressure medication, significantly boosts the cancer drug olaparib — potentially extending its benefits well beyond the BRCA-related tumors it currently treats.
key_points: Researchers found the blood pressure drug telmisartan significantly improves the performance of the cancer drug olaparib.
This pairing could extend olaparib's benefits beyond patients with BRCA-related tumors.
Preclinical studies showed strong immune-boosting and anticancer effects from the combination.
The telmisartan-olaparib combination is already being tested in human clinical trials.
content_html: Drug repurposing — finding a new use for a medicine already proven safe — is one of the more efficient paths to a new cancer treatment, and researchers say they've found a promising one. Telmisartan, a blood pressure drug already taken by millions of people, appears to significantly boost the performance of the cancer drug olaparib.
extra_html: As ScienceDaily reports, that combination showed strong immune-boosting and anticancer effects in preclinical studies, and the appeal goes beyond the lab result: olaparib's clearest benefits have so far been limited mostly to patients with BRCA-related tumors, and pairing it with telmisartan could extend meaningful benefit to a much wider group. The combination is already being tested in human clinical trials — a sign researchers see enough promise to move past mice, though it's still a trial in progress rather than an approved treatment.
